chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, existed and there was nothing other than Him, and He has never ceased to be Knowing of what will occur — and His knowledge of it before its occurrence is like His knowledge of it after its occurrence.'

key_terms.عَالِماً: Knowing, All-Knowing — refers to the divine attribute of 'Ilm (knowledge)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: 'Azza wa Jalla — Mighty and Majestic, an honorific formula for God
key_terms.كَوْنِهِ: Its being/occurrence/existence — from the root k-w-n (to be, to exist)
key_terms.لَمْ يَزَلْ: He has never ceased — emphatic formula denoting eternal continuity of a divine attribute

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about Allah's knowledge before and after events in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrates a statement attributed to the Imam before him (likely Imam al-Sajjad AS), asserting that Allah alone existed before creation with no other thing, and that His knowledge is eternal and unchanging — what He knows of future events is identical to what He knows after they occur. This hadith addresses the attribute of divine pre-eternal knowledge ('ilm al-azali), affirming that God's knowledge is not conditioned by time, unlike human knowledge which updates upon experience. The early Muslim community debated whether divine foreknowledge differed in nature from retrospective knowledge; this narration affirms their absolute equivalence.
